textos.expedicoes_039: No flash at night and no drones near nests.
textos.expedicoes_040: Keep your distance from the animals: no calling, cornering or feeding them.
textos.expedicoes_049: A short trip for beginners, with flat trails and lots of birds near the water.
textos.expedicoes_053: Vast open grasslands, where the giant anteater is often seen.
textos.expedicoes_057: Rocky grasslands and palm swamps; the best time for the maned wolf is at dusk.
textos.expedicoes_059: Photography trips in Cerrado protected areas, always with a local guide and rules for responsible wildlife watching.
textos.expedicoes_063: Maned wolf walking through the grassland
textos.expedicoes_066: Wildlife photography expeditions in the Cerrado: Chapada dos Veadeiros, Emas National Park and Brasília National Park.
textos.galeria_068: The largest toucan. Despite its size, the bill is light and helps control body temperature.
textos.galeria_071: Its loud call, heard from far away at dawn, is one of the most typical sounds of the Cerrado.
textos.galeria_074: Lives in pairs and nests in hollows of dead palm trees, such as the buriti.
textos.galeria_078: Uses its long tongue, up to 60 cm, to eat ants and termites. It has no teeth.
textos.galeria_081: The largest canid in South America. It hunts at night and also eats lots of fruit, such as the wolf apple, helping to spread the seeds.
textos.galeria_087: Click a photo to enlarge it. The badge marks species listed as threatened by ICMBio, Brazil's wildlife agency.

textos.index_105: Trips in small groups, with a local guide and a focus on watching without disturbing the animals.
textos.index_107: 3major river basins start here: the Amazon, the São Francisco and the Paraná
textos.index_109: 2ndlargest biome in Brazil, after the Amazon
textos.index_110: It is the most species-rich savanna in the world and, at the same time, one of the biomes that has lost the most native vegetation in Brazil.
textos.index_113: Some of the animals that turn up most on our expeditions.
textos.index_116: Photographs of animals from Brazil's second-largest biome, to bring people closer to nature and help protect it.

textos.index_121: Photographs of the wildlife of the Brazilian Cerrado, to bring people closer to nature and help protect it.
textos.sobre_126: The palette comes from the biome itself: the brown of tree trunks, dry grass and earth. Every colour was tested with the WCAG contrast formula: dark colours carry white text and light ones, black text.
textos.sobre_128: Wildlife enthusiasts, photographers and students connected to nature.
textos.sobre_130: To show nature to people, helping them connect with wildlife, so as to protect it and prevent its extinction.
textos.sobre_132: A wildlife photography company that wants people to get to know — and want to protect — the animals of the Cerrado.
